_doc: BOATZ economy definition — resources, goods, recipes, and the derived tuning block. Loaded by server/simHost.js, deep-cloned into world.rules/world.economy, and injected into the pure sim (game/sim/*). All numbers are per sim-second unless noted. Values are derived for provable stability (see the plan's Stage 1 / mathematician analysis); change with care and re-run tests/stability.test.js.

tuning._doc_separation: Light ship-to-ship collision avoidance (separation.js), a nod to the rules of the road. SHIP_SEPARATION_RANGE — hulls closer than this get a gentle radial shove apart (SHIP_SEPARATION_PUSH units/substep) so they never stack; kept small (a hull's click radius is ~22) so it is a nudge, not a big buffer. SHIP_AVOID_RANGE — the wider look-ahead within which a hull CLOSING on another ahead eases to STARBOARD (SHIP_AVOID_VEER units/substep): head-on both veer right (pass port-to-port), crossing the give-way vessel (other on its starboard) yields while the stand-on holds, an overtaker keeps clear. SHIP_AVOID_FWD_COS — how far off dead-ahead still counts as a meeting. Only ships under way are touched; a hull and its chase target (`_prey`) are exempt from the polite give-way (a boarding action grapples, it doesn't yield right-of-way). SHIP_COLLIDE_RANGE — the HARD anti-stack floor underneath all of it: no two at-sea hulls may ever overlap closer than this, not even a fighting pair (a final per-substep position correction), so combatants trade fire across a gap instead of welding hull-to-hull. Keep it well under COMBAT_STANDOFF (80) so a clean broadside never trips it.
tuning._doc_island_nav: ISLAND AVOIDANCE (navigation.js) — hulls steer AROUND landmasses in their path instead of sailing through them. ISLAND_RADIUS/_K/_POW mirror the client's WorldRenderer.islandRadius (land radius = ISLAND_RADIUS·clamp((k/ISLAND_RADIUS_K)^ISLAND_RADIUS_POW, 0.4, 1.85)) so a hull rounds the DRAWN island — keep them in step with game/config.js. SHIP_ISLAND_CLEARANCE — how far outside the shore a hull skims; SHIP_ISLAND_LOOKAHEAD — how far ahead it looks for a blocker (kept modest: local greedy avoidance for a sparse ocean of convex islands, not global pathfinding). The destination island is exempt (a ship must enter it to dock). Set SHIP_ISLAND_CLEARANCE to null to disable.
tuning._doc_chronicle_beats: Quiet-life chronicle BEATS (events.js/ship.js) — low-tier ('log') milestones that fill a per-entity Story tab without flooding the news crawl. GOLDEN_CIV/GOLDEN_DAYS: a golden age = civ held ≥ GOLDEN_CIV for GOLDEN_DAYS days (rarer than a BOOM). POP_MILESTONES: population tiers logged once on an upward crossing. PEACE_DAYS: days a port must stay untroubled (no blight/plague/famine/rebellion/haven/high-danger/high-lawlessness) to log a long peace. FIRST_YEAR_DAYS: a magistrate's first unbroken stretch of order. SHIP_VOYAGE_MILESTONES: completed-voyage counts a ship logs.
tuning._doc_scout_shop: Purposeful recon: an idle/thin-trade ship scouts potential SUPPLIERS of what its home lacks rather than aimlessly. A producer of a good the home is actively OVERPAYING for — cheapest KNOWN source >= SCOUT_PRICE_TRIGGER × base (soughtSupply) — is weighted most (×SCOUT_SUPPLY_WEIGHT); a producer of any needed good less so. When shopping, the staleness bar drops to SCOUT_SEEK_STALE days so a motivated buyer re-checks sooner. Only redirects otherwise-idle ships — never perturbs committed trade.
tuning._doc_intel: Information travels only by sea (intel.js): beyond price, an island learns another port's danger (pirate sightings), haven status, and food distress ONLY from docking ships. INTEL_STALE_DAYS — a danger sighting decays to nil over this many days (old trouble is assumed cleared). INTEL_HAVEN_FORGET — a haven sighting is trusted this long, then discounted (may have been redeemed). INTEL_FORGET_DAYS — intel older than this is dropped. INTEL_MAX_SUBJECTS — per-book cap on remembered ports (the scaling guard toward ~1000 islands). SIGHT_RANGE_AT_SEA — a sailing ship sees a port's live facts firsthand within this range (why a captain holds fresher info than the home port). CAPTAIN_REROUTE_MIN_SKILL — a captain this skilled will proactively skip a stop it firsthand-knows has fallen to a haven.
tuning._doc_ledger: Outstanding-voyage ledger (voyages.js): a home port does NOT instantly know a ship was sunk out at sea — it keeps EXPECTING it back until it is overdue. VOYAGE_GRACE_DAYS is the slack beyond the estimated return before a missing ship is presumed lost (and only THEN does the port know to seek a replacement). Until then the lost hull still counts toward the port's believed fleet, so it doesn't over-order — and a pirate that sank it has delayed that knowledge.
tuning._doc_storm_condition: STORMS now BATTER a ship's condition rather than coin-flipping it dead (Phase 4). Inside a storm, each substep hull loses STORM_HULL_DMG_PER_DAY and rig STORM_RIG_DMG_PER_DAY × the storm's intensity × elapsed days, mitigated by the captain's SEAMANSHIP (a master mariner takes far less of the battering). A hull beaten to 0 founders; STORM_SINK_PER_DAY is now only a rare catastrophic KNOCKDOWN (× intensity × hullRisk — a leaky hull is likelier to be thrown down). A poor navigator is BLOWN OFF COURSE: STORM_LOST_CHANCE × intensity × (1−seamanship) per day sets ship.adrift. An ADRIFT ship sails a wandering heading making no real progress (still eating its stores), is easy prey, and founders more readily (maybeSink ×LOST_FOUNDER_MULT). It REGAINS BEARINGS on a daily LOST_RECOVER_BASE + seamanship roll (+LOST_SIGHT_BONUS when land is within SIGHT_RANGE_AT_SEA), then re-plans its voyage. Weathering a storm earns XP_STORM; regaining bearings earns XP_LOST_RECOVER. JURYRIG_PER_DAY — a seamanlike captain mends hull/rig AT SEA from Wood/Fiber carried aboard, a slow patch that gets a cripple home.
tuning._doc_combat_xp: A merchant captain earns experience by completing voyages; a pirate or privateer earns it by FIGHTING. XP_PER_PRIZE — a raider taking a merchant (or sacking a port); XP_PER_KILL — a privateer running down a pirate; XP_PER_DEFENSE — winning a skirmish over a haven. So a feared raider (the 'Redhand' you follow across the map) and a celebrated hunter both climb the ranks the longer they survive, and that rising SKILL feeds back into their decisions: a seasoned captain hunts/watches over a wider reach (PIRATE_SKILL_REACH / PRIVATEER_SKILL_REACH — ±this fraction of the range across the skill span, neutral at average skill) and presses fights a green hand would decline (PIRATE_DEFEND_SKILL_EDGE lowers a defender's odds bar with skill; PRIVATEER_SKILL_NERVE lowers a hunter's caution bar).
tuning._doc_grievance: GRIEVANCE (0..1) — the accumulated resentment of a populace ruled by force. Every rebellion a magistrate CRUSHES (rather than yielding to) leaves a scar: grievance rises GRIEVANCE_PER_QUELL. It makes the NEXT revolt come sooner (REBEL_GRACE_GRIEVANCE), harder to crush (QUELL_GRIEVANCE_MAG), and raises the port's steady LAWLESSNESS (LAWLESS_GRIEVANCE) — so a ruler who only ever bloodily suppresses dissent digs his own grave, and a chronically-misruled island slides toward the black flag. It HEALS slowly (GRIEVANCE_HEAL_PER_DAY, faster the more prosperous/content the port), is largely vented by an OVERTHROW (the hated ruler is gone: ×GRIEVANCE_OVERTHROW_KEEP), and is reset toward HAVEN_REDEEM_GRIEVANCE when a haven is retaken.
tuning._doc_ambition: Magistrate ECONOMIC AGENDAS. Each ambition reshapes the island's stock targets (via AMBITION_BIAS, or for 'industry' the raw inputs of whatever it produces, ×AMBITION_INDUSTRY_INPUT_MULT) — which drives its imports/exports beyond survival — and carries a success signal that buoys or (on overreach amid ruin) erodes the magistrate's loyalty. Food targets are never biased below base (survival floor).
tuning._doc_lawless: LAWLESSNESS (0..1) — civil order on an island (distinct from loyalty, which is political). Drifts toward a steady state set by hardship (poverty/famine/pirate danger raise it) minus governance (a skilled, honest, firm magistrate holds order). Drags civ and population growth, and is the metric a pirate haven grows from / is redeemed by (later).
tuning._doc_blockade: BLOCKADE — a fed pirate with no prey at sea doesn't camp a wharf (which pins the port's whole fleet in harbour and gridlocks trade); it declares a BLOCKADE: ORBITS the port at BLOCKADE_RANGE, chasing any merchant that comes within BLOCKADE_SNAP (its prey range shrinks to the snap while blockading, so it holds station instead of chasing distant traffic), and raises the port's danger BLOCKADE_DANGER/day (drawing privateers) — held for BLOCKADE_DAYS. Captain character shapes it: a WANDERLUST pirate (trait >= WANDER_TRAIT) never blockades — it roves the whole hunt range for moving trade; a BOLD pirate (>= BOLD_TRAIT) blockades TIGHT and raids readily; a TIMID one (<= TIMID_TRAIT) keeps a loose standoff and FLEES a privateer within FLEE_PRIVATEER_RANGE; a GREEDY pirate ignores prizes worth under GREED_MIN_PRIZE.
tuning._doc_pirate_flight: SELF-PRESERVATION & FIGHT-OR-FLIGHT (piracy.js) — a raider weighs its own hide BEFORE pressing a hunt, so it doesn't chase a prize while being shot to pieces. PIRATE_FLEE_HULL — the hull below which a captain of AVERAGE nerve breaks off the hunt to run for a haven and mend; PIRATE_FLEE_HULL_BOLD spreads that threshold across boldness (the bold press on with a staved-in hull, the timid sheer off at the first serious wound). When a pirate-HUNTER bears down (within PIRATE_FLEE_PRIVATEER_RANGE·reach), every raider now decides fight-or-flight: it STANDS to fight only if its strength ≥ the hunter's × an odds bar set by character — PIRATE_FIGHTBACK_ODDS at average nerve, widened by PIRATE_FIGHTBACK_BOLD so the bold engage even at a disadvantage and the timid only a plainly weaker foe (skill sharpens the read via PIRATE_DEFEND_SKILL_EDGE); otherwise it BREAKS OFF and runs for its nearest haven (mend + shelter). A siege right off the raider's own den is left to HAVEN DEFENCE, which contests those waters rather than fleeing them.
tuning._doc_shore: SHORE BATTERIES (shore.js) — an armed island fires on hostile shipping loitering within PORT_CANNON_RANGE, once per PORT_CANNON_COOLDOWN seconds. A lawful port shells PIRATES: its garrison is its armoury (stock.Weapons), each salvo spends PORT_CANNON_COST powder (a Weapons sink, so it falls silent when disarmed and a port under PORT_CANNON_MIN_WEAPONS can't fire). A HAVEN shells besieging PRIVATEERS: its garrison is its entrenchment (havenStrength·PORT_CANNON_FULL), worn down by the bombardment it already takes. Each salvo burns PORT_CANNON_BURN off the target's guns and sinks it with chance PORT_CANNON_SINK·min(1, garrison/PORT_CANNON_FULL). Set PORT_CANNON_RANGE null to disable. Tunable knobs for how hard ports/dens bite back.
tuning._doc_attrition: COMBAT AS ATTRITION (Phase 3) — a fight is no longer one dice roll but a running battle of BROADSIDES, one per COMBAT_ROUND_SEC. Each round both ships fire: HULL & RIG take damage ∝ the OTHER's combatStrength (armour-divided), and both burn COMBAT_WEAPON_BURN powder — so guns run dry and offense fades in a long fight. COMBAT_DMG_BASE — condition removed from an evenly-matched foe per round (×2·strength-share, so an even duel strips ~this from each). COMBAT_CHAIN_FRAC — the fraction of a PIRATE's fire aimed at the RIG (cripple-and-board); COMBAT_CHAIN_MERCHANT — a MERCHANT aims even higher at the rig (DEFENSIVE fire: shoot away the pursuer's sails so she can FLEE, only occasionally landing a hull shot → the rare fend-off); COMBAT_CHAIN_NAVY — a privateer/navy pounds the HULL (out to sink, not flee). combatStrength now reads the GUNNERY facet, adds COMBAT_BOLD_AGGRO×(boldness-0.5) (bold crews fight harder), and is dragged down by a battered hull (×(1 - COMBAT_HULL_STRENGTH_W×(1-hull))). Mid-fight a captain STRIKES her colours (hull ≤ STRIKE_HULL or morale ≤ STRIKE_MORALE, unless bold/gunner) → boarded & plundered; or BREAKS OFF (flees) when outmatched below BREAKOFF_ODDS and the rig can still run. A hull driven to 0 founders outright. The old flat sink rolls (PIRATE_SINK_ON_LOSS/FEND, PRIVATEER_LOSS_SINK, PORT_CANNON_SINK) survive only as an occasional coup de grâce / scuttle.
tuning._doc_flee: FIGHT OR FLEE (assessFlee, piracy.js) — the running assessment BOTH combatants make EACH ROUND (pirate, privateer, any captain in a duel): keep trading blows, or sheer off while she still can? A captain breaks off only when the odds AND his hull have BOTH turned against him — never on either alone (a stout ship trades blows when outgunned; a battered one presses on while still winning). At an AVERAGE captain (boldness & skill 0.5) the two bars are exactly FLEE_HULL and BREAKOFF_ODDS; character only widens the spread around that. NERVE = (boldness-0.5) + (skill-0.5)·FLEE_SKILL_NERVE lowers the hull bar by NERVE·FLEE_NERVE_HULL and the odds bar by NERVE·FLEE_NERVE_ODDS, so the bold & seasoned hold on through worse. The FEARLESS (boldness ≥ COMBAT_FEARLESS) never quit a fight; a DISMASTED ship (rig ≤ RIG_DISTRESS) can't run and must fight on or strike. A privateer that breaks off keeps clear for COMBAT_BREAKOFF_RESPITE sim-seconds before it re-engages (so a mauled hunter actually disengages instead of re-acquiring the same raider and fighting to the bottom).
tuning._doc_prize: PRIZE CAPTURE (Phase 6) — the endgame of a fight. When a merchant STRIKES to a pirate, the raider may take the HULL itself, not just her cargo: a prize crew mans her and she sails under the black flag (and soon seeks a haven, growing the pirate fleet). Gated by PRIZE_CHANCE × the raider's gunnery & boldness (a skilled, bold crew can man a prize), the hull being worth taking (> PRIZE_MIN_HULL), and the fleet-fraction cap (canTurnPirate — capture stays self-limiting). A prize sails with a green skeleton crew (PRIZE_CREW_MORALE). The mirror: when a PRIVATEER beats a pirate it may RECOVER the hull (PRIZE_RECOVER_CHANCE) and return her to its commissioning port as a lawful vessel restored to trade (if the port has a berth) — otherwise the raider is sunk as before.
tuning._doc_combat_round: COMBAT_ROUND_SEC — the reload/re-engage cadence for a pirate↔privateer duel. Without it a privateer's hunt resolves every 0.05s substep, so a caught pirate (or a pirate charging a besieged haven) vanishes on contact. Spacing the exchanges by this many sim-seconds turns a hunt into a running battle that unfolds over a few seconds — both ships trade broadsides, burn guns, and either may be crippled — which is what makes a haven siege read as a battle rather than a frozen line. PIRATE_DEFEND_ODDS — a pirate charges a haven's besieger only if its own strength is at least this fraction of the besieger's; outmatched, it SHADOWS at a menacing distance instead of a suicidal charge. HAVEN_DEFEND_RANGE — the ring around a haven within which pirates rally to its defence and a besieging privateer clears the screen before battering the walls.
tuning._doc_arming: MERCHANT SELF-DEFENCE (ship.js armForDefence + goals.js) — a trader captain DECIDES how many guns to mount from judgment, personality, and the KNOWN danger of the planned route. defensiveArmTarget = ARM_WEAPONS_BASE + [(1-boldness)·ARM_WEAPONS_CAUTION (the cautious always carry some) + routeDanger·ARM_DANGER_BONUS·(0.5+judgment) (known peril, sharpened by the captain's Command judgment)] · (1 - greed·ARM_GREED_THRIFT) (a greedy captain grudges hold space to powder, saving it for saleable cargo — she runs light and trusts her heels), CAPPED at weaponCap·ARM_DEFENSE_CAP_FRAC so a trader is never a warship (it fights DEFENSIVELY — chain-shot at the rig to flee, see COMBAT_CHAIN_MERCHANT — never out-gunning a pirate). routeDanger is belief-based (believedDanger over the voyage's stops, blended with any raider physically off the home port) — no omniscience. Guns load first from the HOME armoury (an operating cost, like provisioning); if the route is dangerous (≥ ARM_BUY_MIN_DANGER) and the home is short by ≥ ARM_BUY_MIN_SHORTFALL, the captain BUYS the shortfall at a Weapons producer already on the route.
tuning._doc_condition: SHIP CONDITION (repair.js) — two 0..1 tracks a hull carries: HULL (structural integrity → combat HP, founder risk at sea & in storms, storm survival) and RIG (sails → speed). Both wear from combat/storms and are MENDED AT PORT from WOOD (hull) and FIBER (rig) — new, sustained demand ports near dangerous waters feel most. RIG_SPEED_FLOOR — a fully-dismasted hull still crawls at this fraction of speed (never frozen → no softlock). RIG_DISTRESS — at/below this rig a ship is 'adrift, dismasted', a distress state aid answers. HULL_LEAK_RISK — a battered hull founders more readily: maybeSink odds ×(1 + this×(1-hull)). Hull-class ARMOR divides incoming damage (a galleon shrugs off what staves a sloop). Repair: REPAIR_WOOD_PER_HULL/REPAIR_FIBER_PER_RIG units to fully mend a track; REPAIR_PER_DOCK caps the fraction mended per port call (a big refit takes a couple of docks), widened by seamanship (REPAIR_SKILL_BONUS); a port keeps REPAIR_RESERVE of its own timber/canvas (home mends free, a foreign yard sells at ask).
tuning._doc_privateer_budget: PROPORTIONAL NAVY — the commissioned privateer force tracks the ACTUAL threat, not the fleet cap. The economy funds about PER_PIRATE hunters per pirate at large + PER_HAVEN per haven under siege; above that budget no port commissions another, and a SURPLUS privateer with nothing in reach stands DOWN early (back to honest trade) rather than idling on the treasury. Without this the navy balloons to PRIVATEER_MAX_FRAC and stays there long after piracy is crushed — over-crushing piracy into invisibility AND draining dozens of traders from the sea. MAX_FRAC is now just the hard ceiling.
tuning._doc_privateer_patrol: PATROL — a commissioned privateer with no pirate to chase doesn't moor at the wharf; it PATROLS, orbiting the port it GUARDS (_guard, the port that commissioned it) at PATROL_RANGE, and INTERCEPTS any pirate that comes within WATCH_RANGE of that port (wider than its raw hunt range — it is actively watching, not just reacting when a pirate wanders into gun-range). Captain character: a BOLD privateer (trait >= BOLD_TRAIT) gives chase far and takes uphill fights; a cautious one holds a tighter patrol and only presses a pirate when the odds are favourable (its strength >= foe's * TIMID_ODDS), shadowing until the raider weakens or overreaches.
tuning._doc_privateer_food: A privateer crew eats and can starve like any other (crew.js) — but unlike a merchant it never docks to reprovision through the trade machine. RESUPPLY valve: when its provisions fall below PRIVATEER_RESUPPLY_DAYS it breaks off station (siege or patrol) and runs for its guard port to victual free (the state feeds its own navy), the same way a starving pirate makes for a haven — hunger is a real forcing function on both factions, not a merchant-only concern.
tuning._doc_merchant_defence: A threatened merchant FLEES for the nearest safe port and lets her stern guns cripple the pursuer's RIG to cover the run (defensive fire resolved when the chase closes to gun-range — she never stands to slug it out, being no warship). A bold, seasoned captain (MERCHANT_RUN_BLOCKADE_TRAIT on boldness+seamanship) will instead RUN THE BLOCKADE — hold her course past a raider — but ONLY if she is not clearly outgunned by it (own combatStrength ≥ raider's × MERCHANT_STAND_ODDS); outmatched, even a bold captain flees. So arming buys a covered retreat, not a licence to stand and be boarded.
tuning._doc_haven: PIRATE HAVENS — a failed island whose LAWLESSNESS stays maxed falls to the black flag: a stronghold that HARBOURS pirates (they resupply food + fence plundered loot there), BUILDS new pirate ships from that fenced wealth (nothing free), and which PRIVATEERS assault to REDEEM back into a lawful port. Grows from the lawlessness stat (see mayoral-goals), self-limiting via privateer suppression + a hard cap. HAVEN_PRESSURE_RECOVER — a port on the brink recovers its civic order SLOWLY (pressure builds +1/failing-day but eases only this much per relief-day), so a genuinely-failed island still tips over even through the odd good day. HAVEN_FIRST_BUILD_GRACE_DAYS — how soon after falling a haven can lay its first hull. An assault lands at most ONCE PER DAY per haven (see havens.js), so breaking a den takes a privateer holding station for days — during which the haven builds/harbours pirates (the drama).
tuning._doc_rescue: AID AT SEA (Phase 5) — the mercy valve, and where the diplomatic layer becomes PHYSICAL: a passing ally heaves-to for a crippled ship. Detection: a ship in DISTRESS (repair.js inDistress — dismasted rig, or adrift) is a beacon; a captain notices one within RESCUE_RANGE and will divert up to RESCUE_DIVERT_MAX (trait-scaled: the generous go farther, the greedy grudge the time). INFO BY SEA: he judges the relationship from a CARRIED ally-set (ship._allies/_embargoes, snapshotted from HOME's rep at departure — never a live rep read at sea), so he may help a home his own has SINCE fallen out with, or pass one it has since befriended. He aids a fleetmate (same home) always, a carried ally, never a carried embargo. A cautious captain (low boldness) won't heave-to where local danger > RESCUE_DANGER_MAX (pirate waters suppress mercy). He gives only SPARE Fiber/Wood/Food (beyond RESCUE_KEEP_* and his own crew's victuals) — RESCUE_*_BATCH each — patching the victim's rig/hull and topping up food+morale. Reputation lands AT THE QUAY, not mid-ocean: the deed is recorded aboard and bumpRep(REP_AID_GAIN) fires only when the helper next reaches home and reports (like recordTrade) — so goodwill propagates by sea. A helper rests RESCUE_COOLDOWN_DAYS between rescues; the deed earns XP_RESCUE (seamanship + command).
